name: efcore
description: Entity Framework Core 10.0.13 on Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL 10.0.3 and Npgsql 10.0.3. Native mode uses Database.BeginTransactionAsync, SaveChangesAsync, CommitAsync, and RollbackAsync, with Pooling off so a commit's backend is still visible at after-end. execute-sql uses Database.ExecuteSqlAsync for the unique violation only. pooled uses an NpgsqlDataSource with MaxPoolSize 1 for TX-03. Category C faults throw from an EF Core transaction interceptor before Npgsql sends ROLLBACK or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT. Migrations use Database.MigrateAsync and the history table ef_migrations_history. The adapter does not add its own advisory lock around Migrate.

modes.description: Database.BeginTransactionAsync, CommitAsync, and RollbackAsync. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. The native TX-01A violation is SaveChangesAsync, which EF Core wraps in a savepoint. Nested scopes use CreateSavepointAsync. Pooling is false. EnableRetryOnFailure is not called. The provider's default execution strategy is left in place.

The same BeginTransactionAsync and CommitAsync calls. The marker is still SaveChangesAsync. The unique violation is Database.ExecuteSqlAsync, which is not wrapped in the savepoint EF Core creates around SaveChangesAsync. TX-01A only, plus the observation controls.

The same context and transaction calls. NpgsqlDataSource with MaxPoolSize 1 is passed to UseNpgsql. The context is disposed between the two TX-03 units, which returns the connection to the pool. The pool is not cleared and this adapter does not issue a validation query. TX-03 only, plus the observation controls.

TX-04.independent-inner.reason: EF Core has no propagation mode that promises an independent transaction while an outer transaction stays open. BeginTransactionAsync throws if a transaction is already in progress. A second DbContext is a second physical transaction coordinated by application code, not a framework propagation mode. This adapter does not manufacture that mode.

TX-05.managed-serializable.reason: EF Core has no managed transaction API that runs a callback and commits when the callback returns, and that accepts an isolation level. ExecutionStrategy.ExecuteAsync is a retry policy. AutoTransactionBehavior starts an implicit transaction around SaveChanges and does not take an isolation level. BeginTransactionAsync is the explicit API and is the other case.
